NET-01.binary_question: Are security zones defined to segment the network?
NET-01.pass_condition: At least 3 distinct zones are configured (e.g., trust, untrust, DMZ)
NET-01.fail_condition: Only default zones exist or zones are not meaningfully segmented
NET-01.remediation: Define security zones aligned to network segments: trust (internal), untrust (internet), DMZ, management. Apply zone protection profiles.

NET-01.binary_question: Is the default inter-zone traffic policy set to deny?
NET-01.pass_condition: Default security policy denies all inter-zone traffic not explicitly permitted
NET-01.fail_condition: A catch-all allow rule exists at the bottom of the rulebase or default action is not deny
NET-01.remediation: Remove catch-all allow rules. Enforce deny by default. Implement explicit allow rules for required business flows only.

NET-02.binary_question: Does any active security rule permit any source, any destination, and any service?
NET-02.pass_condition: No active rule has source=any AND destination=any AND service=any with action=allow
NET-02.fail_condition: One or more active rules allow any source, any destination, any service
NET-02.remediation: Replace any-any-any allow rules with specific rules limited to required source zones, destination zones, applications, and services. Document business justification for each rule.

NET-02.binary_question: Do any active rules have zero hits in the last 90 days?
NET-02.pass_condition: No active rule has zero hit count after 90+ days of operation
NET-02.fail_condition: One or more active rules have not matched any traffic in 90 days
NET-02.remediation: Review rules with zero hits. Disable or remove rules with no business justification. For new rules, implement a 30-day review cycle.

NET-02.binary_question: Do rules use application-default or specific services rather than 'any' service?
NET-02.pass_condition: All allow rules specify application or restrict service to application-default
NET-02.fail_condition: Rules use service=any without application identification restrictions
NET-02.remediation: Replace service=any with application-based controls or specific port/protocol definitions. Enable App-ID on all rules.

NET-02.check_name: Inbound Internet Rules to Internal Zone
NET-02.binary_question: Are there rules allowing direct inbound internet access to internal/trust zones?
NET-02.pass_condition: No rules allow untrust-to-trust traffic without explicit destination address restriction
NET-02.fail_condition: Rules permit inbound internet traffic to broad internal address ranges
NET-02.remediation: Restrict inbound internet traffic to specific published services in DMZ. Use NAT to expose only necessary services. Block direct inbound access to internal/trust zones.

NET-03.binary_question: Are threat prevention security profiles attached to all allow rules that handle external or untrusted traffic?
NET-03.pass_condition: All allow rules handling external traffic have antivirus, anti-spyware, and vulnerability protection profiles attached
NET-03.fail_condition: One or more allow rules handling external/untrusted traffic have no threat prevention profile attached
NET-03.remediation: Attach a security profile group containing antivirus, anti-spyware, vulnerability protection, and URL filtering profiles to all allow rules handling external or untrusted traffic.

NET-03.binary_question: Is an active antivirus security profile configured and applied?
NET-03.pass_condition: At least one antivirus profile exists with action=drop/reset on malware detections and is applied to relevant rules
NET-03.fail_condition: No antivirus profile exists or it is set to alert-only with no block action
NET-03.remediation: Create a strict antivirus profile with action=drop for viruses and reset for spyware. Enable WildFire integration. Apply to all rules handling external or inter-zone traffic.

NET-03.binary_question: Is a vulnerability protection profile configured and applied to relevant rules?
NET-03.pass_condition: Vulnerability protection profile exists with block actions for critical and high severity threats
NET-03.fail_condition: No vulnerability protection profile or it only alerts on high/critical without blocking
NET-03.remediation: Configure a strict vulnerability protection profile: critical=reset-both, high=reset-both, medium=drop. Apply to all perimeter and inter-zone allow rules.

NET-04.binary_question: Is traffic logging enabled on all active security policy rules?
NET-04.pass_condition: All allow rules have log-end (and optionally log-start) enabled
NET-04.fail_condition: One or more allow rules have logging disabled
NET-04.remediation: Enable log-end on all security policy allow rules. For high-sensitivity rules enable log-start also. Configure log forwarding profiles to send logs to SIEM.

NET-04.binary_question: Is a log forwarding profile configured to send logs to a SIEM or syslog server?
NET-04.pass_condition: A log forwarding profile exists, is configured with a SIEM/syslog destination, and is applied to security rules
NET-04.fail_condition: No log forwarding profile configured or profiles are not applied to security rules
NET-04.evidence_source: Log Forwarding Profile and Server Profile Export
NET-04.remediation: Create a log forwarding profile with syslog server destinations pointing to your SIEM. Apply the profile to all security policy rules. Verify log receipt at the SIEM.

IAC-01.binary_question: Are local administrator accounts limited to the minimum required?
IAC-01.pass_condition: Three or fewer local admin accounts exist; no shared admin accounts
IAC-01.fail_condition: More than 5 local admin accounts or shared admin credentials exist
IAC-01.remediation: Limit local admin accounts to break-glass/emergency use only. Integrate with RADIUS/LDAP for centralized authentication. Remove shared or service accounts with admin privileges.

IAC-01.binary_question: Is the default 'admin' account active or using the default password?
IAC-01.pass_condition: Default admin account is renamed, disabled, or has a unique strong password
IAC-01.fail_condition: Default 'admin' account exists and is active
IAC-01.remediation: Rename or disable the default admin account. Create named individual accounts for all administrators. Enforce strong password policy.

IAC-01.binary_question: Do administrator accounts have role-based access profiles rather than all superuser access?
IAC-01.pass_condition: Admin accounts are assigned custom roles with least-privilege permissions
IAC-01.fail_condition: All admin accounts have superuser or full administrative access
IAC-01.remediation: Create custom admin role profiles that limit each admin to their required functional area (e.g., read-only, network-only, security-policy-only). Assign appropriate roles to each administrator.

IAC-07.check_name: MFA Not Enforced for Admin Access
IAC-07.binary_question: Is multi-factor authentication enforced for all administrator logins?
IAC-07.pass_condition: All admin accounts use an authentication profile with MFA (RADIUS+OTP, SAML, certificate)
IAC-07.fail_condition: Admin accounts use password-only authentication without MFA
IAC-07.remediation: Configure an authentication profile with RADIUS+OTP or SAML to enforce MFA. Apply the profile to all admin accounts. Disable password-only authentication for admin access.

IAC-07.check_name: MFA Not Enforced for GlobalProtect VPN
IAC-07.binary_question: Is MFA enforced for GlobalProtect VPN authentication?
IAC-07.pass_condition: GlobalProtect gateway authentication profile requires MFA
IAC-07.fail_condition: VPN authentication uses password-only or certificate-only without MFA
IAC-07.remediation: Configure GlobalProtect to use an authentication profile with MFA. Integrate with RADIUS, SAML, or LDAP+OTP. Enforce certificate + credential authentication for highest security.

LOG-01.binary_question: Is syslog configured to forward system logs to a centralized log server?
LOG-01.pass_condition: Syslog server profile exists and is assigned in device logging settings
LOG-01.fail_condition: No syslog server configured or syslog profiles are not applied
LOG-01.evidence_source: Syslog Server Profile and Device Logging Configuration
LOG-01.remediation: Configure a syslog server profile with your SIEM IP/port. Apply the profile to all log categories: system, config, traffic, threat, hipmatch, and audit.

LOG-01.binary_question: Are configuration change events logged with committer identity?
LOG-01.pass_condition: Configuration audit log is enabled and captures admin identity, timestamp, and change summary
LOG-01.fail_condition: Configuration change logging is disabled or not forwarded
LOG-01.evidence_source: Commit Audit Log and Device Logging Configuration
LOG-01.remediation: Enable configuration audit logging under Device > Log Settings. Forward config audit logs to SIEM. Require individual admin accounts (not shared) so committer identity is captured.

CFG-01.binary_question: Has a security hardening baseline (CIS Benchmark or vendor guide) been applied?
CFG-01.pass_condition: Device configuration shows evidence of hardening: management restrictions, secure protocols, strong passwords
CFG-01.fail_condition: Default configuration with no hardening controls applied
CFG-01.remediation: Apply the CIS Benchmark for Palo Alto Networks or Palo Alto IRON hardening guide. Restrict management access, disable unused services, enforce strong authentication.

CFG-01.binary_question: Are weak TLS versions (1.0, 1.1) or cipher suites prohibited on SSL/TLS service profiles?
CFG-01.pass_condition: SSL/TLS service profiles enforce TLS 1.2 minimum with strong cipher suites
CFG-01.fail_condition: TLS 1.0 or 1.1 is permitted in SSL/TLS service profiles
CFG-01.remediation: Update all SSL/TLS service profiles to enforce TLS 1.2 as minimum. Disable weak cipher suites (RC4, DES, 3DES, NULL, MD5). Apply strict profiles to management interface and GlobalProtect.

CFG-02.binary_question: Do commit messages reference an approved change ticket?
CFG-02.pass_condition: All commit log entries include a change ticket number or reference
CFG-02.fail_condition: Commits exist without change ticket references or with generic/empty descriptions
CFG-02.remediation: Enforce a change management policy requiring all commits to reference an ITSM ticket. Train administrators to include ticket numbers in commit descriptions. Implement Panorama automation to validate ticket references.

CFG-03.check_name: Management Interface Exposed to Untrusted Networks
CFG-03.binary_question: Is management interface access restricted to approved management IP ranges?
CFG-03.pass_condition: Management interface has permitted-IP list configured and management traffic is restricted to dedicated management network
CFG-03.fail_condition: Management interface permits access from any IP or from internet-facing networks
CFG-03.remediation: Configure permitted-IP list on management interface. Place management interface on a dedicated out-of-band management network. Disable management access from data-plane interfaces.

CFG-03.binary_question: Are unused management services (Telnet, HTTP, SNMP with defaults) disabled?
CFG-03.pass_condition: Only necessary management services are enabled: HTTPS, SSH. Telnet, HTTP disabled.
CFG-03.fail_condition: Telnet, HTTP, or SNMP with default community strings are enabled
CFG-03.remediation: Disable Telnet and HTTP on management interfaces. Use HTTPS and SSH only. Change SNMP community strings from defaults. Configure SNMPv3 with authentication.

CHG-01.binary_question: Are all configuration changes traceable to an approved change record?
CHG-01.pass_condition: Commit log shows all changes include ticket references and named committer identities
CHG-01.fail_condition: Changes exist without ticket references or performed outside change window
CHG-01.evidence_source: Commit Audit Log and ITSM Change Records
CHG-01.remediation: Implement a change freeze process. Configure Panorama to require commit descriptions. Integrate with ITSM to validate change tickets before commits are applied.

CRY-01.check_name: Weak TLS Permitted in Decryption Profile
CRY-01.binary_question: Do SSL decryption profiles block connections using deprecated TLS versions?
CRY-01.pass_condition: Decryption profiles block SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 and enforce strong cipher suites
CRY-01.fail_condition: Decryption profiles permit weak TLS versions or do not enforce cipher restrictions
CRY-01.remediation: Update decryption profiles to block connections using SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1. Exclude weak cipher suites (RC4, DES, NULL, EXPORT). Enable certificate verification.

IRO-01.check_name: No Threat Alert Forwarding to SIEM
IRO-01.binary_question: Are threat log events forwarded to a SIEM for incident detection?
IRO-01.pass_condition: Threat logs are forwarded to SIEM via syslog/log forwarding profile with alert on high/critical severity
IRO-01.fail_condition: Threat logs are local only and not forwarded to SIEM or alert platform
IRO-01.evidence_source: Log Forwarding Profile and Threat Log Configuration
IRO-01.remediation: Create a log forwarding profile that sends threat logs to your SIEM. Configure the SIEM with correlation rules to alert on high and critical severity threats within 15 minutes of detection.
